# GEO report: Millstone Bakery **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 100/100, Strong Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. All ten scored rules that apply came out Clear, read from code. Nothing is unknown inside the repository. The only open question is whether your host or a firewall changes what crawlers receive (see "Can't tell from code"). ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first Nothing is broken, so these three are the biggest open unknowns and the best ideas. ### 1. Confirm real crawlers can reach the site - **Why it matters:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall in front of the site blocks search and AI crawlers. - **Where:** your host's access log (outside the repo) - **What the code says:** `robots.txt:2`: `Allow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 100 if it comes back clear. A blocked crawler would be a hosting problem. It would not change the code score, which stays 100. ### 2. Add the hero image, or fix its path - **Why it matters:** the home page points at an image that isn't in the repository, so the picture might not show. - **Where:** `index.html:16` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 100. The score doesn't change, because the alt text is already present. I only checked the git-tracked files, so a build step might add the file. ### 3. Say where and when you're open - **Why it matters:** visitors, and tools answering "where is Millstone Bakery?", get no address or hours from any page. - **Where:** `index.html:15` - **What the code says:** `

We bake a wide range of loaves from heritage grains. Pre-order for weekend collection.

` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 100. This is optional and doesn't affect the score. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `robots.txt`: valid groups, tiny, has a `Sitemap:` line | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `robots.txt:1-3`: `*` allows `/`. Only `/members/` is blocked | | GEO-014 | Pages can be indexed | Clear | `/`, `/breads.html` and `/classes.html` have no noindex. `/members/` has noindex, is not in the sitemap and is not linked from the nav | | GEO-015 | Canonical URLs | Clear | `index.html:8`, `breads.html:8`, `classes.html:8`: one absolute URL each on the declared origin | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Clear | Plain static HTML, all text is in the source | | GEO-004 | Structured data (JSON-LD) valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Clear | `sitemap.xml` is valid and `robots.txt:8` points to it | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | All 4 pages have `lang="en"` and a unique title and description | | GEO-016 | Pages linked in server HTML | Clear | Every page has `` links in its nav | | GEO-017 | Snippet limits vs AI-search policy | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0`. `breads.html:16` uses `data-nosnippet`, which is a deliberate choice | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | `index.html:16` has alt text, every page has a title, and the links have text | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not an app | | GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | Not present | | GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | Not an app | ## Other problems found None found. ## Worth considering - **Put the address and opening hours on a page and label them as structured data:** `index.html:6`: `Millstone Bakery, sourdough in York`. No page gives a street address or hours. Add them as text, then describe them with `Bakery` or `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD. That might help tools answer "where is it, and when is it open?". - **Back up "Over twenty loaves":** `breads.html:15`: `Over twenty loaves through the week, including our seeded rye and the country white.` The page names two loaves. List them all with a short description each, or give each loaf its own page and sitemap entry. - **Give each class a date, price and length:** `classes.html:15`: `Book early, because places go quickly.` The page has no schedule, price, group size or way to book. Those are the things a visitor would ask. - **Explain how pre-ordering works:** `index.html:15`: `Pre-order for weekend collection.` Nothing says how to order or the cut-off time. - **Add Organization/WebSite structured data:** nothing states the site's name or links in machine-readable form, even though the nav and title show them. - **Add `` dates to the sitemap:** `sitemap.xml:3-5` has only `` entries. - **Add social tags and a 404 page:** none of the `` sections has `og:title` or `og:description`, and there is no `404.html`. ## Can't tell from code - **Server responses:** the status codes for `/robots.txt` and the pages, and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers, come from the host. A live check would show them. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Training crawlers:** `robots.txt:5-6` blocks `GPTBot`. That matches `trainingCrawlers: "block"` in your config. I didn't count it. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find the public pages, as `geo.config.json` says (`aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`). - `/members/` is deliberately private. It has both `Disallow` in `robots.txt` and `noindex` in the page. - I read all 7 tracked files: 4 pages, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and `geo.config.json`. There's no package.json, no build step and no JSON-LD. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
